notes: Memories can be edited. A memory written by the model is a first draft — it misspells a name, gets a detail the wrong way round, or is true but so vague it is no use — and until now the only options were to leave it wrong or delete it and type the whole thing again. Tap the pencil on any memory card, or just tap the memory itself, and an editor slides up with the current wording ready to change. It says plainly that what is in the box is word for word what gets sent to that character, because it is. The same editor now handles writing a new memory, replacing the old pop-up box that was awkward to type into on a phone, and it carries a toggle for whether the memory is always sent, so pinning no longer means saving first and hunting for the star afterwards. Editing changes the wording and nothing else: the date stays as the day the memory was learned, since rewording it does not change when you said it, and the card notes that it was edited so you can tell your corrections from the model's own notes at a glance.
